prompt: Hypothetical. OBV starts at 0. Closes Rs 100 (volume 10,000), Rs 103 (volume 20,000) and Rs 101 (volume 5,000). What is the OBV after the third close?
solution: Day 2 close is higher, so add 20,000. Day 3 close is lower, so subtract 5,000. OBV = 0 + 20,000 - 5,000 = 15,000.

prompt: Hypothetical. Bar 1: typical price Rs 200, volume 1,000 shares. Bar 2: typical price Rs 206, volume 3,000 shares. What is the VWAP?
Hypothetical. OBV starts at 0. Day 1: higher close, volume 12,000. Day 2: lower close, volume 7,000. Day 3: lower close, volume 3,000. What is the OBV after day 3?
solution: Day 1 adds 12,000, so OBV = 12,000. Day 2 subtracts 7,000, so OBV = 5,000. Day 3 subtracts 3,000, so OBV = 2,000.

prompt: Hypothetical. A stock closes lower than the day before on a volume of 40,000 shares. What happens to OBV?

explanations.a: OBV adds volume only when the close is higher than the day before. This close is lower.
explanations.c: OBV stays the same only when the close is equal to the day before. This close is lower.
explanations.d: OBV does not double. It adds or subtracts the day's volume, and this day's close is lower.

prompt: Hypothetical. A stock falls 2 percent on a day with very high volume. A reader writes, 'High volume on a down day means the price will keep falling tomorrow.' Which response fits the book's rules?

options.text: Agree. Heavy selling always leads to more falls
Volume shows how many shares traded, not which way the price will go. The forecast is not supported by the volume alone
Volume on a down day is never recorded, so the reader is wrong for a different reason
Ignore the volume, because it has no meaning for any day

explanations.a: Volume does not show direction or what comes next. Heavy trading on a down day can be followed by a rise, a fall or a flat period.
explanations.c: Volume is recorded on down days, just as on up days. This option is factually wrong.
explanations.d: Volume is useful for describing how much traded. It is only wrong to treat it as a forecast.

prompt: Read this statement. Which part is wrong? 'VWAP is a moving average of closes that adds up each day. It resets at the start of each session. Its weight at each price is the volume traded there.'

options.text: VWAP is a moving average of closes that adds up each day
It resets at the start of each session
Its weight at each price is the volume traded there

explanations.b: This part is correct. VWAP restarts at the start of each session in the book's definition.
explanations.c: This part is correct. Each typical price is weighted by the volume at that bar, so more volume means more weight.

prompt: Which statement about VWAP fits this book?

options.text: It predicts the price of the next session
It restarts each session and is used only in an optional intraday module, on paper
It is the same measure as a daily-bar average of closes
It measures the price change over one month

explanations.a: VWAP does not predict. Its predictive value is not established, and the book does not treat it as a forecast.
explanations.c: A daily-bar VWAP is a different measure, and it is not the same as an average of closes. Check the definition in Kite.
explanations.d: VWAP is a session measure. It is not a one-month price change.
